messages.subject: Unwarranted does not converge error
parts:
First of all, here is my code:

SEM_Model <- '
Default ~ Property.Type + Geographic.Location + Loan.Size + Number.of.Properties + DSCR + LTV
Loss ~ Property.Type + Geographic.Location + Loan.Size + Number.of.Properties + DSCR + LTV
'
SEM_Output <- sem(SEM_Model, data = DataSet, ordered=c("Default", "Loss"), control=list(iter.max=100))

I get this error:

Error in solve.default(B) : 
  system is computationally singular: reciprocal condition number = 8.87184e-30

Now the reason why this should be a legitimate model is:

1) The univariate analyses (logistic regressions of the two dichotomous dependent variables Default and Loss) produce valid results with most variables having p-values of 0 (three stars). The Somers D' (measure of concordant pairs between model implied results and actual results is 80% for Default and 97% for loss). 

2) This is all fake data to figure out how to do the regressions so I can eventually use legitimate data. The data set was constructed with both a deterministic and stochastic component so as to replicate real-life randomness in addition to the natural influences of each factor. Each of the exogenous variables has a tangible linear effect on Default and Loss. The random part ensures that the regression will never achieve complete separation. But ultimately, it is fake (but realistic) data. 

Property Type and Geographic Location are categorical variables. Number of Properties is ordinal. The rest are continuous.

I will provide data if needed, but there's gotta be something else at play here because there is a relationship I am already aware of in the data, the SEM just breaks.
